column2: Amsterdam is a city in the Netherlands^It has many canals^Waterways helped shape its streets and neighbourhoods~The Amstel flows through Amsterdam^The city grew beside the water^A dam on the river helped give Amsterdam its name~Narrow houses stand beside canals^Many have tall fronts^Limited space influenced the shapes of old canal-side buildings~Bicycles are common in Amsterdam^Many people cycle for daily journeys^Cycle routes help connect homes with work and schools~Some canal houses lean towards the street^Goods were lifted from above^Hooks near the roofs helped workers move heavy loads

Berlin is a city in Germany^The Spree flows through it^The river connects several parts of the city~Berlin has many parks and lakes^The Tiergarten is one large park^Green spaces provide places to walk and rest~The Brandenburg Gate is a city landmark^Its columns frame a broad gateway^It was completed in the eighteenth century~The Berlin Wall divided the city^It no longer forms that barrier^The border opened in 1989 and parts remain as historical sites~Museum Island has several important museums^They stand near the Spree^Their collections allow visitors to explore different periods and cultures

Paris stands beside the Seine^It is a city in France^Bridges connect neighbourhoods on the river's two banks~The Eiffel Tower is made of iron^It rises above the city^It opened for the world fair in 1889~The Louvre is a large museum^It was once a royal palace^Its collections include works from many places and periods~Île de la Cité is a river island^It lies in central Paris^Notre-Dame Cathedral stands on this island~Paris has an extensive underground railway^People call it the Métro^Its first line opened in 1900

London is a city in England^The Thames flows through it^Its river helped connect the city with trade by sea~Bridges connect the Thames banks^Tower Bridge is one example^Its central sections can lift to let taller vessels pass~London has many large parks^Hyde Park is one of them^These open spaces provide places for walking and wildlife~The Underground carries people across London^Parts run beneath the streets^Its first railway opened in 1863~Big Ben is a large bell^It sits inside a clock tower^People often use its name for the whole tower

Madrid is a city in Spain^It stands on inland high ground^It is far from Spain's main sea coasts~The Manzanares flows through Madrid^Parks follow parts of its banks^The river is much smaller than many major European city rivers~The Prado displays important paintings^It is a major art museum^Its collections include works by Velázquez and Goya~The Retiro is a large park^People walk beside its lake^Its gardens developed from a former royal landscape~Madrid has a central square called Sol^Many streets lead towards it^Nearby markers connect with Spain's radial road network

Moscow is a city in Russia^The Moskva flows through it^The river bends around parts of the city centre~The Kremlin is a fortified complex^Walls surround its historic buildings^It stands beside the river in central Moscow~Red Square lies beside the Kremlin^Large public buildings face the square^Saint Basil's Cathedral stands at one end~Moscow has a large metro system^Many stations have elaborate interiors^The first line opened in 1935~The city's streets include ring routes^They circle the centre^Their pattern reflects the city's long outward growth

Rome is a city in Italy^The Tiber flows through it^Bridges connect districts on both riverbanks~The Colosseum is an ancient amphitheatre^Large crowds once gathered there^Its surviving walls show the scale of Roman public buildings~Ancient Romans built many aqueducts^They carried water towards settlements^Some remains can still be seen around Rome~The Roman Forum was a public centre^People met and traded there^Its ruins preserve traces of buildings from different periods~Vatican City lies within Rome's urban area^It is a separate small state^Saint Peter's Basilica stands within that state

Ulaanbaatar is a city in Mongolia^Mountains surround its valley^The Tuul River flows through the wider city region~The city has very cold winters^Summers are much warmer^Its inland position contributes to strong seasonal temperature contrasts~Some neighbourhoods include traditional ger homes^These are round felt-covered dwellings^Other districts have apartment buildings and modern offices~The city developed from a mobile monastery^Its settlement moved several times^It became established at its present location in the eighteenth century~The Gandan monastery is a city landmark^Its buildings remain in religious use^Visitors can learn about important Mongolian Buddhist traditions there

Lisbon is a city in Portugal^It stands beside the Tagus estuary^Its waterfront opens towards the Atlantic Ocean~Hills rise above the waterfront^Streets climb between neighbourhoods^Viewpoints look across roofs and river water~Trams travel through parts of Lisbon^Some run along narrow streets^They form part of the city's public transport network~Painted tiles decorate many buildings^They are called azulejos^Their patterns can show both decoration and historical scenes~An earthquake damaged Lisbon in 1755^A tsunami and fires followed^The rebuilt centre developed a planned street pattern

Dublin is a city in Ireland^The Liffey flows through it^The river reaches Dublin Bay on the Irish Sea~Bridges connect the riverbanks^The Ha'penny Bridge is one example^Its name recalls a former toll charged to people crossing~Dublin has a long literary history^Many writers are associated with it^James Joyce and Samuel Beckett are two examples~Phoenix Park is a large city park^People walk and cycle there^A herd of fallow deer also lives within the park~Trinity College keeps the Book of Kells^It is an illustrated medieval manuscript^Its decorated pages were created more than a thousand years ago

Hong Kong lies on China's southern coast^It includes islands and mainland areas^Its landscapes combine dense urban districts with country parks~Victoria Harbour separates two busy shores^Ferries carry people across the water^Hong Kong Island and Kowloon face each other across the harbour~Steep hills rise behind city buildings^Roads and paths climb their slopes^Victoria Peak provides views across parts of the urban area~Hong Kong has an extensive rail network^Trains connect many districts^Ferries and buses provide other important links~Much of Hong Kong is not skyscrapers^Beaches and wooded hills lie nearby^Country parks protect substantial areas beyond the busiest streets

Shanghai is a city in China^It lies near the Yangtze's mouth^Its position connects inland river routes with coastal trade~The Huangpu runs through Shanghai^The Bund stands beside it^Buildings there reflect the city's history as a major port~Tall towers rise in Pudong^They stand across the river from the Bund^The skyline shows a different period of urban development~Shanghai has a large metro network^Many daily journeys use its trains^The network connects both older and newer districts~Yu Garden preserves a traditional garden landscape^Its design uses rocks and water^The garden began in the sixteenth century

Istanbul has European and Asian sides^Water separates them^The Bosphorus runs between these two parts of the city~Ferries link the opposite shores^Passengers cross alongside busy ship traffic^Bridges and rail links also connect the two sides~The city was once called Constantinople^It served as an imperial capital^Its history connects Roman and Byzantine and Ottoman periods~Hagia Sophia has a huge central dome^It stands in the historic city^Its building has served different religious roles over the centuries~The Grand Bazaar contains many covered passages^Shops line its walkways^Its trading history began in the fifteenth century

Almaty is a city in Kazakhstan^Mountains rise close to it^The nearby peaks belong to the northern Tian Shan region~Almaty was once Kazakhstan's capital^The capital moved in 1997^It remains an important cultural and economic city~Apple trees have strong local connections^Wild apples grow in nearby mountains^The region helped contribute to the ancestry of cultivated apples~The city has parks and tree-lined streets^People use them for walking and shade^These green spaces contrast with the snowy peaks nearby~High mountain valleys lie above Almaty^Medeu is one well-known place^Its skating rink stands in a mountain setting outside the centre

Beijing is a city in northern China^It has a long history^Its urban layout includes both historic areas and modern districts~The Forbidden City has many courtyards^Palace buildings stand around them^It served as an imperial palace for centuries~Hutongs are traditional city lanes^Homes stand beside these narrow passages^Some historic neighbourhoods preserve courtyard-house layouts~The Temple of Heaven stands in parkland^Its buildings have distinctive round forms^It was used in imperial ceremonies connected with harvests~Great Wall sections lie outside Beijing^Mountains carry many surviving walls^Visitors must travel beyond the city centre to reach them

Dubai stands beside the Persian Gulf^It is a city in an emirate^The emirate belongs to the United Arab Emirates~Dubai Creek crosses older urban districts^Small boats carry people across it^Trade developed around this sheltered waterway~The Burj Khalifa is a very tall tower^It has many different floors and uses^It opened in 2010~Palm Jumeirah is an artificial island^Its shape resembles a palm tree^Placed materials changed part of the city's coastline~Desert landscapes lie beyond the dense city^Sand dunes form part of them^The contrast between coast and desert helps shape the wider region

Seoul is a city in South Korea^The Han River flows through it^Bridges link districts on the opposite banks~Hills and mountains surround the city^Paths lead through some of them^Their slopes provide green spaces near dense urban districts~Gyeongbokgung is a historic palace^Its buildings stand around courtyards^The palace was first established in 1395~Some areas preserve traditional hanok houses^Their roofs have curved edges^These neighbourhoods show a different urban form from apartment towers~Seoul has a large rail network^Many residents use it daily^The system connects the city with surrounding metropolitan areas

Bangkok is a city in Thailand^The Chao Phraya flows through it^The river has long supported movement and settlement~Boats carry people along the river^Ferries connect opposite banks^Some piers also connect with urban rail services~Canals run through parts of Bangkok^People call them khlongs^They record an important part of the city's water-based history~Wat Arun stands beside the river^Its central tower is a landmark^The temple's surface includes decorative ceramic pieces~The city combines old and new buildings^Historic shop houses stand beside modern districts^Some older buildings are being reused for creative work

Delhi is a large urban region^It lies in northern India^New Delhi forms one part of this wider territory~The Yamuna runs through Delhi^It is part of the Ganges system^The river has influenced settlement and farming nearby~The Red Fort has large defensive walls^Its buildings served Mughal rulers^Construction began under Shah Jahan in the seventeenth century~Old Delhi has busy narrow streets^Markets fill many of them^The area preserves a different layout from planned New Delhi~New Delhi contains many national institutions^It is not all of Delhi^Keeping these two names distinct helps describe the place accurately

Recife is a city in Brazil^It lies on the Atlantic coast^Its centre includes islands and riverbanks~Bridges link parts of the city^Waterways pass between neighbourhoods^The Capibaribe is one important river in Recife~The city's name means reef^Reefs lie near parts of the coast^These rock and marine features helped shape its harbour~Historic buildings stand in Recife Antigo^This is part of the old centre^Its streets reflect centuries of Atlantic trade~Frevo is a local music and dance tradition^Dancers use quick movements^Small colourful umbrellas are associated with its performances

Mumbai is a city in India^It stands beside the Arabian Sea^Its sheltered harbour supported the growth of a major port~The city grew across former islands^Land reclamation joined them together^Seven islands formed the core of the historic island city~Suburban trains carry many commuters^They connect homes with workplaces^Rail travel is an important part of everyday movement~The Gateway of India faces the harbour^Its arch stands beside the waterfront^It was completed in 1924~Mumbai has a major film industry^Studios and creative workers are based there^Hindi-language cinema is one important part of the city's cultural life

New York is a city in the USA^It stands beside a large harbour^The Hudson River reaches the sea beside the city~The city has five boroughs^Manhattan is one of them^The others are Brooklyn and Queens and the Bronx and Staten Island~The Statue of Liberty stands on an island^It faces the harbour^The statue was dedicated in 1886~Central Park lies within Manhattan^Paths cross its green spaces^Its designed landscape includes lakes and wooded areas~New York has an extensive subway system^Trains connect many neighbourhoods^It carries people between places above and below ground

Cairo is a city in Egypt^The Nile flows through it^Bridges connect districts across the river~The Nile supports life in dry surroundings^Green fields grow beside its waters^Desert landscapes begin beyond much of the river valley~Historic Cairo has many old buildings^Some stand along narrow streets^Its architecture records important periods of Islamic history~The Giza pyramids lie near Cairo^They are ancient royal tombs^Giza is across the Nile from much of central Cairo~Cairo's museum collections preserve ancient objects^These include sculptures and everyday items^Such objects help explain life along the Nile over many centuries

Manila is a city in the Philippines^It lies beside Manila Bay^The Pasig River reaches the bay through the city~Intramuros is Manila's historic walled district^Old walls surround parts of it^Its name comes from words meaning within the walls~The harbour connects Manila with sea routes^Ships carry goods and passengers^Its coastal position helped support the city's growth~Jeepneys are a familiar transport vehicle^They carry passengers on city routes^Their designs grew from vehicles adapted after the Second World War~The wider metropolitan area includes many cities^Manila is one of them^The city and Metro Manila do not have identical boundaries

Toronto is a city in Canada^It stands beside Lake Ontario^The lake forms part of the Great Lakes system~The CN Tower rises above the skyline^It is a tall communications tower^It opened to the public in 1976~Islands lie near the waterfront^Ferries connect them with the city^Their parks provide views back towards the skyline~Toronto has many different language communities^People have moved there from many places^Food and cultural events reflect these varied connections~Streetcars travel along several city roads^They form part of public transport^Subways and buses provide other links across the city

Dakar is a city in Senegal^It stands on an Atlantic peninsula^The peninsula reaches west from mainland Africa~The ocean borders several city districts^Fishing and port work are important^Its position connects Senegal with Atlantic sea routes~Gorée Island lies offshore^Ferries connect it with Dakar^Its historic buildings are connected with a difficult Atlantic history~Markets sell many everyday goods^Visitors can see fabrics and food^Markets also serve the practical needs of local residents~Dakar has a strong arts scene^Music and visual art are important^Its festivals and museums connect local work with wider audiences

Panama City lies on Panama's Pacific side^It stands near the canal's entrance^Ships travel between this region and the Caribbean side~The Panama Canal connects two oceans^Locks raise and lower ships^The waterway crosses the narrow Isthmus of Panama~Casco Viejo is a historic district^Its streets contain old public buildings^It developed after an earlier city was destroyed in 1671~Modern towers line parts of the waterfront^They contrast with the old districts^The skyline reflects the growth of a major service and trading city~Tropical habitats lie near the urban area^Forests shelter many kinds of wildlife^Soberanía National Park protects land near the canal region

Reykjavik is a city in Iceland^It stands near the Atlantic coast^It is the country's capital and largest city~Geothermal water helps heat many buildings^Hot water rises from underground^This resource reduces the need to heat homes with fuel~Hallgrímskirkja is a church on a hill^Its tower is a city landmark^The design recalls shapes associated with Iceland's volcanic landscapes~The city has very different summer daylight^Winter days are much shorter^Its northerly latitude creates strong seasonal light changes~The name recalls a smoky bay^Early settlers saw rising steam^Geothermal steam helped inspire the place's name

Bogotá is a city in Colombia^It stands high in the Andes^Its elevation gives it a cooler climate than many tropical lowlands~The city sits on a broad high plain^Mountains rise along its eastern edge^This setting shapes the direction of urban growth~La Candelaria is a historic district^Its streets include old buildings^Museums and public institutions occupy parts of this area~The Gold Museum displays worked gold objects^Many were made before European colonisation^The collections show skilled metalworking by different Indigenous societies~Cycle routes connect parts of Bogotá^Some roads close for cycling events^The city's Ciclovía offers public space for active travel

Jakarta is a city on Java^It lies beside the Java Sea^Its low-lying coastal position affects drainage and flooding~Several rivers cross the urban area^Canals help carry water towards the coast^Managing these waterways is important for nearby communities~Kota Tua preserves parts of old Batavia^Historic buildings stand around its square^The area records part of the city's port history~Commuter trains connect surrounding districts^Many residents make long daily journeys^The metropolitan area extends beyond Jakarta's own boundaries~The Thousand Islands lie offshore^The name refers to an island group^Some islands have coral habitats within the Java Sea

Los Angeles is a city in California^It lies near the Pacific coast^Mountains and valleys shape its wider urban region~The city spreads across a broad area^Many neighbourhoods have different characters^Roads and railways link this large metropolitan landscape~Hollywood is connected with film production^Studios developed across the wider region^Film and television remain important parts of local cultural life~The Los Angeles River crosses the city^Much of it has engineered banks^Projects aim to improve some river habitats and public spaces~The Griffith Observatory overlooks the city^Visitors can learn about the sky^It opened in 1935

Vancouver is a city in Canada^It lies near the Pacific Ocean^Mountains rise north of its sheltered coastal waters~The city has a busy port^Ships carry goods through nearby waters^Its position connects inland transport with Pacific sea routes~Stanley Park has forests and paths^Its seawall follows much of the shore^The park lies beside the central urban area~Rain is common in cooler seasons^Nearby mountains receive snow^Ocean air influences the region's relatively mild coastal climate~Vancouver hosted the Winter Olympics in 2010^Whistler hosted several mountain events^The games used venues across the wider region

This city lies in southern Vietnam^The Saigon River flows beside it^Its waterways connect with the wider southern lowlands~The city was formerly called Saigon^That name is still widely used^Its official name changed in 1976~Markets are important city meeting places^They sell food and everyday goods^Bến Thành is one well-known market in the centre~The port connects with regional waterways^Goods move between land and water^Trade has long influenced the city's growth~Older buildings stand beside modern towers^They record different periods of development^The urban landscape reflects continuing changes in work and travel

Miami is a city in Florida^It lies beside Biscayne Bay^The Atlantic Ocean is beyond the nearby barrier islands~Miami Beach is a separate city^Bridges connect it with Miami^The two names do not describe identical municipal areas~The region has warm subtropical conditions^Summer rain is important^Coastal communities also prepare for tropical storms~Spanish is widely used in Miami^The city has strong Latin American connections^These links influence food and music and everyday life~The Everglades lie west of the city^Their wetlands support varied wildlife^Water management connects urban needs with this fragile environment

Singapore is an island city-state^It lies near the equator^It stands at the southern end of the Malay Peninsula~Its port connects busy sea routes^Ships carry goods between many regions^The nearby Strait of Malacca is an important maritime passage~Gardens and trees grow among dense buildings^Parks provide shade and public spaces^Urban planning includes connected green areas~Hawker centres bring food stalls together^People share tables in these public spaces^Their food traditions reflect several cultural communities~Freshwater is carefully managed here^Rainwater collection is one source^Recycling and desalination also contribute to the water supply

Buenos Aires faces a wide estuary^It is a city in Argentina^The broad estuary opens towards the Atlantic Ocean~The historic centre grew near a port^Trade influenced the city's development^Waterfront districts record this connection with shipping~Tango has deep local roots^Music and dance developed in the region^Buenos Aires and nearby Montevideo share parts of this history~Wide avenues cross parts of the city^Narrower streets fill many neighbourhoods^Different districts show different periods of urban growth~The Río de la Plata is an estuary^It looks much wider than many rivers^Fresh river water mixes with Atlantic waters farther downstream

Mexico City lies in a high basin^Mountains surround the urban area^Its elevation helps keep temperatures cooler than nearby tropical lowlands~The city grew over former lake landscapes^Water once covered much of the basin^Changes to drainage helped reshape the city's ground and waterways~Tenochtitlan stood here before modern Mexico City^It was a major Mexica city^Its remains survive beneath and beside later buildings~The city has a large metro network^Many residents travel by train^Rail transport connects dense urban districts~Xochimilco preserves canals and growing areas^Farmers use land called chinampas^These agricultural landscapes connect with the basin's long water history

Rio de Janeiro is a coastal city^It lies in Brazil^Mountains stand close to its beaches and bays~Sugarloaf Mountain rises beside the harbour^It has a rounded rocky shape^Cable cars carry visitors towards its summit~Christ the Redeemer stands above the city^The statue is on Corcovado^It was inaugurated in 1931~Tijuca Forest covers nearby mountain slopes^It provides habitats within the urban region^Parts of the forest were restored after earlier clearing~Rio has a strong carnival tradition^Music and dance fill the celebrations^Samba schools prepare large performances for the annual event

Sydney is a city in Australia^It lies beside a large harbour^The Pacific Ocean borders its eastern coastal suburbs~Sydney Harbour has many bays and inlets^Ferries connect different shores^Waterways shape journeys across the wider city~The Opera House has sail-like roof forms^It stands beside the harbour^It officially opened in 1973~The Harbour Bridge crosses the water^Trains and road vehicles use it^It opened in 1932~Aboriginal histories long predate the modern city^Different local communities have deep connections here^Their stories remain important to understanding the harbour landscape

Addis Ababa is a city in Ethiopia^It stands in the highlands^Its elevation gives it a cooler climate than many nearby lowlands~Entoto rises above the city^Its slopes have paths and woodland^The mountain area is connected with the city's early development~The city is a major transport centre^Roads connect it with other regions^Its airport links Ethiopia with many international routes~The African Union has its headquarters here^Representatives gather in the city^This gives Addis Ababa an important role in regional diplomacy~The name means New Flower^It comes from Amharic^The city developed in the late nineteenth century

Lima is a city in Peru^It stands near the Pacific coast^The Andes rise farther inland~The Rímac flows through Lima^Its water comes from mountain regions^Managing river water is important in this dry coastal setting~Rainfall is very low in many months^Coastal mist is common in cooler seasons^Ocean conditions help shape this unusual desert-city climate~The historic centre has many old buildings^Some have enclosed wooden balconies^Their architecture reflects the city's colonial history~Ancient settlements existed before colonial Lima^Their remains survive within the modern city^Huaca Pucllana is one archaeological site surrounded by urban districts

Tokyo is a city in Japan^It stands beside Tokyo Bay^The wider metropolitan area occupies a broad lowland plain~The city was once called Edo^Its name changed in 1868^Tokyo became closely connected with the modern imperial government~Railways carry many daily journeys^Stations connect different lines and neighbourhoods^The network extends far into surrounding metropolitan areas~Sensō-ji is a historic Buddhist temple^It stands in Asakusa^Its gates and shopping streets form a well-known city landscape~Tokyo includes more than dense central streets^Western areas have hills and forests^The metropolitan administration also includes islands in the Pacific

Auckland is a city in New Zealand^It lies on the North Island^Its narrow land area stands between major harbours~The city lies within a volcanic field^Several hills are old volcanic cones^These landforms have strong cultural and geological importance~Two large harbours face different waters^Waitematā opens towards the Pacific side^Manukau lies towards the Tasman Sea~Māori communities have deep connections here^Many places have traditional Māori names^Tāmaki Makaurau is the widely used Māori name for Auckland~Sailing is popular on Auckland's waters^Marinas and ferries use its sheltered harbours^These waterways help shape the city's identity and movement

Cape Town is a city in South Africa^It stands beside Table Bay^Mountains rise close to the city and its coast~Table Mountain has a flat-looking top^Cloud sometimes covers its upper surface^Sandstone forms the mountain's familiar cliffs~The Cape Peninsula extends southwards^It has rocky coasts and beaches^The Cape of Good Hope lies near its southern end~Fynbos grows on many nearby slopes^Its plants include proteas^This vegetation belongs to the Cape Floristic Region~Robben Island lies offshore^It has a difficult prison history^Its museum helps visitors learn about apartheid and human rights

Lagos is a city in Nigeria^Its districts surround a lagoon^Bridges connect islands with mainland areas~The Atlantic lies beyond its coastal islands^The city has important port facilities^Water routes helped shape its trading history~Lagos has many different neighbourhoods^Markets serve everyday needs^People move between homes and workplaces across a large urban region~Music and film are important here^Many creative workers are based in Lagos^The city has strong connections with Nigeria's cultural industries~Its name comes from a Portuguese word^That word means lakes^The name reflects early European visitors' impressions of the waterways

Nairobi is a city in Kenya^It stands in the eastern African highlands^Its elevation makes it cooler than many coastal areas~The city developed beside a railway route^Rail transport influenced its early growth^It was founded as a railway depot in 1899~Nairobi National Park lies near the city^Wild animals live within its habitats^The park creates an unusual meeting of urban and wildlife landscapes~The city has important international offices^UN Environment is based here^Nairobi connects local and international environmental work~The name has a Maasai origin^It refers to cool water^This recalls the area's river and highland setting

Perth is a city in Western Australia^The Swan River flows through it^Its western suburbs face the Indian Ocean~Kings Park overlooks parts of the city^It includes native plants and bushland^The park provides views across river and urban districts~Beaches line much of the nearby coast^Ocean conditions shape local weather^The city has hot dry summers and wetter winters~Rottnest Island lies offshore^Ferries connect it with the mainland^Quokkas are among the island's distinctive animals~Perth is far from other large Australian cities^Long distances separate major population centres^Its position gives it strong links with Indian Ocean travel routes

Santiago is a city in Chile^The Andes rise to its east^The city occupies part of a broad inland basin~The Mapocho flows through Santiago^Bridges connect its urban banks^The river begins in mountain areas outside the city~Santa Lucía is a hill in the centre^Paths lead through its landscaped areas^It provides views across surrounding districts~The city has a large metro network^Many people use it for daily journeys^Rail links connect different parts of the metropolitan region~Pacific beaches are beyond the coastal mountains^The ocean is not beside central Santiago^This inland position distinguishes it from Chile's major coastal ports

Suva is a city in Fiji^It lies on Viti Levu^The city stands on the island's southeastern side~Suva has a sheltered harbour^Ships connect it with other islands^The port supports movement across the wider Pacific region~Rain is common in the city^Green hills rise nearby^The southeast receives moist winds from surrounding ocean waters~The Fiji Museum keeps historical collections^It stands in Thurston Gardens^Its objects help explain Fiji's varied cultural histories~Many different communities live in Suva^Their connections shape food and daily life^The city is an important centre for regional Pacific organisations

Honolulu is a city in Hawaii^It stands on the island of Oahu^Its coast faces the Pacific Ocean~Waikīkī is a coastal district^Its beaches attract many visitors^It lies east of central Honolulu~Diamond Head is a volcanic crater^Its Hawaiian name is Lēʻahi^The crater forms a familiar landmark above the coast~ʻIolani Palace stands in Honolulu^It was a royal residence^Its history connects with the former Hawaiian Kingdom~Honolulu has an important harbour^Ships have used these sheltered waters for generations^The name is commonly translated as sheltered harbour

The Appalachians rise in eastern North America^They are an old mountain system^The range extends from the southeastern United States towards Canada~Forests cover many mountain slopes^Rivers run through the valleys^These habitats support many different plants and animals~Mount Mitchell is a high Appalachian peak^It stands in North Carolina^Its summit rises just over 2000 metres above sea level~The mountains have long rounded ridges^Erosion has worn them over time^Their present shape differs from many younger sharp mountain ranges~Related ancient rocks occur across the Atlantic^Scotland has some of these connections^Continents now separated by ocean were once joined

The Mongolian Plateau lies in inland Asia^Much of its land is high^It extends across Mongolia and neighbouring parts of China and Russia~Grasslands cover broad parts of it^Herders raise grazing animals^Open steppe landscapes are important across this region~The Gobi occupies part of the plateau^It includes rock and gravel deserts^Not every dry area is covered with sand dunes~Winters can be very cold^Summers can be warm^The inland position produces strong seasonal temperature differences~Mountains surround parts of the plateau^Many areas stand over 1000 metres high^The Altai and Khentii Mountains form parts of its wider boundaries

The North Sea lies beside northern Europe^Britain lies to its west^Norway and Denmark border its eastern side~Its waters are relatively shallow^They lie above a continental shelf^These shallow seas differ from the much deeper Atlantic basin~Fishing has a long history here^Ports connect coastal communities^Protecting fish stocks matters for future fishing~Strong winds cross the open water^Offshore wind turbines use them^Wind farms now occupy parts of the North Sea~Rivers carry freshwater into the sea^The Rhine is one example^Its water reaches coastal areas shared by several countries

The Tian Shan rise in Central Asia^They contain high snowy peaks^Parts extend across China and several neighbouring countries~Glaciers store water in the mountains^Meltwater feeds rivers below^This water matters to farms and settlements in drier lowlands~Mountain valleys have different habitats^Forests grow on some slopes^Higher areas include alpine grasslands and permanent ice~Jengish Chokusu is the highest summit^It rises above 7000 metres^The mountain stands along the Kyrgyzstan and China border~Different sections have World Heritage recognition^One section was listed in 2013^Western Tian Shan joined the list in 2016

The Himalayas rise across southern Asia^They are very high mountains^The range stretches between the Tibetan Plateau and lower southern plains~Everest is part of the Himalayas^Its summit is above sea level^Nepal and China announced a summit height of 8848.86 metres in 2020~Two tectonic plates push together here^The Indian plate meets Eurasia^Their collision helped raise this great mountain chain~Major rivers begin in these mountains^Snow and ice store freshwater^River systems carry this water towards large populated lowlands~Plants change as the land rises^Warm forests give way to colder habitats^The highest slopes have very little plant growth

The Kazakh Steppe has wide grasslands^It lies across northern Kazakhstan^Its landscapes continue into nearby parts of Russia~Grass grows across large open areas^Trees are less common in drier places^The steppe belongs to a wider Eurasian grassland belt~Herding has a long history here^People have raised grazing animals^Mobile livelihoods developed around the needs of animals and water~Many areas are now used for farming^Crops grow on parts of the steppe^Land use must balance food production and healthy soils~Wildlife needs connected grassland habitats^Saiga antelopes use steppe landscapes^Their migrations show why large open spaces matter

The Urals cross part of Russia^They run roughly north to south^They extend for about 2500 kilometres~The Urals help mark a continental boundary^Europe lies mainly to their west^Asia lies mainly to their east in the usual convention~These are very old mountains^Erosion has worn many peaks down^Their shape differs from much younger mountain systems~Many valuable minerals occur in the Urals^People have mined them for centuries^The region's geology helped support industrial development~Forests grow across many Ural slopes^Northern areas become colder and less wooded^The long range crosses several climate and vegetation zones

The Arabian Desert covers much of Arabia^Its landscapes are very dry^It stretches across much of the Arabian Peninsula~Some areas have enormous sand dunes^The Empty Quarter is one example^Other areas contain rocky or gravel-covered surfaces~Desert animals conserve water^Some rest during the hottest hours^Oryx and sand cats are examples of desert-adapted animals~Oases provide water in some places^Palms can grow beside them^Groundwater has helped support settlements and travel routes~Desert nights can become much cooler^Heat escapes after sunset^Dry air and clear skies help create large daily temperature changes

The Arabian Sea belongs to the Indian Ocean^It lies west of India^Arabia and eastern Africa border other parts of it~Monsoon winds change with the seasons^They affect ships and coastal weather^Sailors historically used these winds for long-distance trading~The Gulf of Aden joins this region^It leads towards the Red Sea^The Bab el-Mandeb connects the gulf with that sea~Many people fish along its coasts^Marine life depends on healthy waters^Currents can bring nutrient-rich water towards the surface~The sea has important shipping routes^Ports connect several surrounding countries^These routes link South Asia with western sea passages

The Rockies rise in western North America^They cross Canada and the United States^The range contains high peaks and deep valleys~Snow collects on many high slopes^It melts during warmer months^This water helps feed rivers that flow into distant regions~The Continental Divide follows many Rocky ridges^Water flows towards different ocean basins^Its direction depends on which side of the divide it falls~Mountain habitats change with height^Forests cover many lower slopes^Higher areas can have alpine meadows and bare rock~National parks protect parts of the range^Banff is one Canadian example^Rocky Mountain National Park protects another area in Colorado

Southern China has many green hills^Rivers pass through their valleys^The region includes landscapes south of the central Chinese plains~Rice grows in warm wet areas^Some fields lie on terraces^Terraces create flatter growing spaces on sloping ground~Limestone hills rise near Guilin^Water dissolves the rock over time^This creates caves and steep-sided karst landscapes~Warm seasons bring substantial rain^Monsoon winds influence the climate^Healthy trees and soils help slow water on steep slopes~People build settlements beside valleys and rivers^These routes connect hilly areas^Waterways have long supported travel and trade in southern China
